questions.question: What does “unified” mean in a healthy AI platform?
options: Consistent identity, metadata, interfaces, evidence, and operations across supported workflows
One model framework and one serving runtime for every workload
A single production cluster with no tenant boundaries
A developer portal that owns every application outcome
questions.explanation: The platform unifies durable contracts. It can support several implementations when they preserve those contracts.

questions.question: Why is a Kubernetes namespace alone insufficient proof of tenant isolation?
options: Network, node, storage, accelerator, secret, data, cluster-scoped object, and upgrade boundaries need separate controls
Namespaces cannot contain workloads
Namespaces always require a dedicated control plane
Namespaces prevent resource quotas
questions.explanation: A namespace is a useful management and authorization scope, but several shared resources and failure paths remain outside it.

questions.question: Eighteen tenants each need 2.5 GPUs at peak, and 40% of their peaks overlap. What is the concurrent GPU demand before packing overhead?
options: 7.2 GPUs
18 GPUs
20 GPUs
45 GPUs

questions.question: Which items must be bound to an evidence-grade release record?
options: Candidate digest, evaluation and lineage, policy version, exposure, approver, and rollback target
Only the mutable production alias
Only aggregate model accuracy and average latency
A dashboard URL and the latest notebook
questions.explanation: A reproducible decision needs immutable behavior identity, the evidence and policy that approved it, bounded exposure, and recovery.

questions.question: A candidate improves aggregate quality by 4.1% but regresses a critical slice by 2.6%. What should the platform do when the slice floor is -0.5%?
options: Hold promotion and investigate or repair the critical-slice regression
Promote because aggregate quality improved
Delete the critical slice from the evaluation
Increase canary traffic to hide sampling noise
questions.explanation: A declared critical-slice floor is a release invariant. Aggregate improvement cannot silently override it.

questions.question: Which set best measures an AI platform as an internal product?
options: Time to first valid deployment, failed-job causes, policy exceptions, utilization, rollback success, and recovery time
Number of internal frameworks and lines of generated YAML
Total dashboard count and cluster count
Number of mandatory migrations completed
questions.explanation: Developer outcomes, resource efficiency, policy friction, and recovery behavior measure whether the platform creates safe operational value.
